clock_quality.rule: fetched_utc = raw linuxReceivedTs (feed receive clock), else raw fetchTs (bridge capture clock): exact. available_utc = fetched_utc (the bridge's own availabilityTs is a few hundred ms earlier and is not used as the pack clock). Rows with neither clock would be published on eventTs; none observed.

columns.meaning: feed observation clock for the row (raw ts unless a capture clock exists in the payload; see rule)
columns.name: fetched_utc

columns.meaning: availability lower bound: = fetched_utc for exact rows, source-stated instant for published rows, null for unvintaged
columns.name: available_utc

columns.meaning: exact | published | unvintaged (see README.md, Clock quality)
columns.name: clock_quality

columns.meaning: raw eventTs = source (MT5) event time = raw ts
columns.name: event_utc

columns.meaning: MT5 symbol exactly as received (GCZ26, XAUUSD, ...)
columns.name: native_symbol

columns.meaning: live | stale (stale = event older than 30 s at receipt or historical replay)
columns.name: status

columns.meaning: Reading.price, USD: (bid+ask)/2 when both present, else last
columns.name: price

columns.meaning: source clock correction applied to sourceEventEpochMs
columns.name: clock_correction_sec

columns.meaning: raw instrumentMetadata (JSON): contract size, exchange, path, tick
columns.name: instrument_metadata_json

columns.meaning: UTC day the feed appended the row (raw file name); availability is never later than the end of this day
columns.name: raw_file_date

columns.meaning: residual raw keys with no typed column (JSON object) or null
columns.name: extra_json

dedup_rule: exact duplicates share (ts, sha256 of scrubbed raw + asset/venue/price/currency/status/source); the first occurrence is kept
name: moneyplant_quotes
notes: Native unit: USD per contract unit as quoted by MT5 (COMEX/NYMEX futures, XAU/XAG spot).
terminalSession (opaque session id) and clockCalibratedTs are dropped; the dated-contract block is always empty in this source and dropped.
The broker account object of the raw rows is removed by the reader; it never reaches a frame.
